text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "SchNet takes the interatomic distance d_ij = ||r_i - r_j|| as the filter network input to keep the filters rotationally invariant [W2726670313#009]. It does not feed the raw distance directly: it expands the distance with radial basis functions e_k(r_i - r_j) = exp(-gamma||d_ij - mu_k||^2), with centers 0 Å ≤ mu_k ≤ 30 Å spaced every 0.1 Å and gamma = 10 Å, which adds a non-linearity that decorrelates the initial filters and speeds training [W2726670313#009]. The expanded distances are then fed into two dense layers with softplus activations to compute the filter weight W(r_i - r_j) [W2726670313#009]. The later SchNet paper describes the same filter-generating network as taking the vector from atom i to neighbor j, which is constrained to respect known invariances [W2778051509#007]."}
